real_conflicts: The proposal to 'shift the title block slightly to the left or right' to break symmetry is a direct violation of the typographic mandate. The centered alignment is not a mistake; it is the visual anchor that provides the 'institutional credibility' required by the brief. Moving the text would destabilize the composition and make the typography look like a floating label rather than a monumental inscription, undermining the 'scientific weight' of the serif typeface.
accepted: The proposal to 'apply a subtle, low-opacity noise or grain texture overlay across the entire canvas' is accepted. This texture will help the typography integrate with the environment by breaking up the sterile digital smoothness, allowing the white text to feel like it is suspended in particulate matter rather than sitting on a flat vector background.
concession: I concede that the current rigid horizontal alignment of the headline is too static for a theme of 'descent.' The text needs to feel like it is being pulled down by pressure, not just placed on a page.
compromise: Instead of shifting the text block off-center, we will apply a very subtle vertical scale distortion to the headline 'BELOW THE LAST LIGHT.' The top of the letters will be slightly wider than the bottom, creating a subtle 'perspective' or 'pressure' effect that mimics the sensation of depth without breaking the centered, authoritative hierarchy.
nonnegotiable: The serif typeface must remain the primary visual voice. It is the only element that bridges the gap between 'scientific curiosity' and 'museum credibility.' Replacing it with a sans-serif or a more decorative font would destroy the tone of the exhibition.
